description: Per-phase gate protocol. Every phase boundary stops, reports what happened, states what comes next, and asks the user to approve, skip, adjust or stop. The user is never surprised by what onestop did, and can redirect at any boundary.
why: onestop's first real end-to-end run completed with 10 of 15 phases silently skipped and the user never told. Two gates at the far ends of a long pipeline meant everything between them was invisible. A gate at every boundary makes the run legible as it happens rather than auditable afterwards.

mechanism.instruction: A gate is a real AskUserQuestion call, not a sentence in prose asking the user to confirm. Prose requests for confirmation get skipped under context pressure - that is exactly how the invisible run happened.
mechanism.record: The engine is the only writer of the ledger: the orchestrator records every answer with gate_record and never edits .onestop/run.json. phase_start refuses to begin a phase while an earlier one is unfinished or awaiting its gate, and refuses implement until its authorising gate is approved. The Stop hook reminds the user when a gate is pending.

every-phase.description: Gate at every phase boundary. Maximum visibility and control - the user sees each step and approves the direction.

milestone.description: Gate at gate zero, at the gate that authorises implementation (plan, upgrade-plan, reproduce, verify-green or review - whichever the run has), after design, after implement, and at ship. Phases in between report in one line and continue.

autonomous.description: Gate zero and ship only. Gate zero authorises implementation. Use when the task is well understood and the user wants the result, not the journey.

gate_modes.always_stop: In every mode: gate zero, ship, a blocked phase, and any phase whose report leaves a decision only the user can make (open:) - a technology, a version, a dependency, an unknown command. A mode decides how often the user approves; it never lets onestop decide for the user.

gate_shape.instruction: Compact by default: the whole run in one line, then only what changed. Expand every phase outcome only at the plan gate and the ship gate.

sections.name: PROGRESS
sections.content: The engine's progress line: every phase in the mask with one mark - ✓ done, ⤼ skipped, ▶ active, ⏸ awaiting its gate, ✗ blocked, · still to come.
sections.rule: Every phase, never a window around the current one. The pending marks are the remaining journey, so the user can redirect early.

sections.name: JUST DID
sections.content: What the phase that just finished produced - files, findings, decisions, numbers - with paths.
sections.rule: Concrete artifacts. 'Discovery complete' is not a report; 'found 3 auth implementations, next-auth dominant at src/auth/options.ts:14' is.

sections.name: DECIDE
sections.content: Every open item the phase's reports returned, batched, each with the recommended answer.
sections.rule: Only when there is something to decide. Technology and version choices always appear here and are never resolved silently.

sections.name: NEXT
sections.content: The next phase, what it will do, and which specialists it dispatches by name.
sections.rule: Name the specialists. The user should know who is about to work and on what.

sections.name: RECOMMEND
sections.content: What onestop advises, and the one-line reason.
sections.rule: Always recommend. A gate that lists options without advising pushes the decision back without helping.

sections.name: OPTIONS
sections.content: Continue / skip / adjust / stop, recommendation first.
sections.rule: Four at most. Free-text redirect is always implicitly available. The question header is 12 characters or fewer.

standard_options.instruction: The default option set at a phase boundary. Adapt the labels to the actual phase - 'Continue to review' beats 'Continue'.

options.label: Skip <next phase>
options.meaning: Move past it to the phase after.
options.must_state: What is lost by skipping. A skip whose cost is unstated is a decision made blind - say plainly what will not be checked, written or verified.

options.label: Adjust first
options.meaning: The user changes scope, approach or plan before this phase runs. Take their input, update the plan and the ledger, then re-present the gate.
options.must_state: Re-present the gate after adjusting so the user confirms the amended direction rather than the original.

options.label: Stop here
options.meaning: End the run. Write the ledger as stopped, and report exactly what exists and what does not.

narration.instruction: Between gates, the user still sees what is happening. Announce each significant action as it starts - not a running commentary, but never silent work either.
announce: Every agent spawned, by name, and what it is working on.
Every parallel wave dispatched, with its lane count.
Every file written or modified - path only, never the contents.
Every decision resolved without asking, with the rule that settled it.
Every command run whose result changes the plan.
do_not_announce: Individual file reads during discovery - report the conclusion instead.
Internal reasoning steps that produce no artifact.
Anything that would repeat what the last gate already said.

skip_policy.instruction: The user may skip any phase except ship. Two skips are never honoured without a second answer, because their cost may not be in mind at that moment - and the engine, not the orchestrator, decides when they apply.

confirm_twice.when: the change surface touched a security trigger, or the intent is security
confirm_twice.say: gate_record returns needs_confirmation naming the surfaces. Show it, ask again, and pass confirmed:true only if the user still skips. The engine records the override.
gate_record returns needs_confirmation: the change would ship with nothing proving it works. Ask again; pass confirmed:true only if the user still skips.

skip_policy.rule: Never refuse a skip. Warn once, with specifics, then do what the user decides; the ledger records that they decided it. Ship cannot be skipped - to keep work out of git, the user chooses "leave uncommitted" at the ship gate.

tier_scaling.instruction: Gate content scales with tier; the gate itself does not disappear. A trivial change still shows the user what it is about to do - it just does it in two lines instead of ten.
tier_scaling.trivial: One-line DONE and NEXT. Options reduce to continue/stop.
tier_scaling.small: Short DONE and NEXT, full option set.
tier_scaling.large: Full gate shape, plus the open decisions the phase surfaced.

no_batching.rule: One gate per phase. ALWAYS. Never combine two or more phases behind a single gate, however little each one had to decide.
no_batching.why: Batching was tried and rejected. On a real run, four analysis phases were combined behind one gate on the reasoning that none of them individually had a decision for the user. The user could no longer see what each phase actually did, which is the precise thing per-phase gating exists to provide. 'Nothing to decide here' is a judgement the user makes, not the orchestrator.
no_batching.enforcement: The Stop hook flags any ledger gate stamp matching a batched pattern, and any two phases sharing one gate value.

gate_zero.name: Classification and phase plan
gate_zero.when: Immediately after classifying the request, BEFORE the first phase runs.
gate_zero.why: The user has to know what kind of task onestop decided this is, and which phases follow from that, before any work happens. A request the user thought was an automation task and onestop classified as a feature will run the wrong pipeline end to end, and the user finds out far too late.
must_state: The detected intent, in plain words - 'this is an automation task', 'this is a bug fix' - not just the id.
Why it classified that way, citing the signals in the request that decided it.
The tier, and what that changes.
The full ordered phase list this intent produces, with any phase that will be skipped and why.
The stack and the specialists that will be bound.
options: It is a different kind of task  (reclassify - the user names the real intent, the phase mask is rebuilt, and this gate is presented again)
Adjust the phase list  (add or drop phases before anything runs)
gate_zero.rule: Never start phase 1 without passing gate zero. Classification is automatic; proceeding on it is not.

blocked.when: A retry budget ran out (build fix, test fix, review fix, dev loop) and the engine blocked the run.
blocked.shows: The last real error, verbatim and short, and every approach tried.
options: Try another approach (adjusted - grants one more round)
